messages.content: Can you analyze the DNA sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" and "AGCTTAGGCTA" using the reference sequence "AGCTTAGCTA" to identify any potential 'insertion' mutations, then repeat the same analysis for 'deletion' and 'substitution' mutations?

function.name: analyze_dna_sequence
function.description: Analyzes the DNA sequence based on a reference sequence and return any potential mutations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sequence.description: The DNA sequence to be analyzed.

mutation_type.description: Type of the mutation to be looked for in the sequence.

For deletion: compare both sequences to reference. First matches, no deletion. Second has no deletion.

Substitution: compare both. First matches, no substitution. Second has one substitution? Wait difference: reference: AGCTTAGCTA. Sequence: AGCTTAGGCTA. At position 7, reference has C? Let's align: reference: A G C T T A G C T A. Sequence: A G C T T A G G C T A. So at position 8 (1-indexed), reference has C, sequence has G. So substitution at position 8. So function will detect.

Thus we need to call function with mutation_type "insertion" for both sequences. Then "deletion" for both. Then "substitution" for both. But maybe we can combine? The function expects a single sequence. We can call it separately for each sequence. Provide results.
